blocks.text: The **Banking Ombudsman** is a senior official appointed by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to settle customer complaints about deficiency in certain banking services. A complaint is entertained only if it falls under the grounds listed in **Clause 8** of the **Banking Ombudsman Scheme 2006** (as amended up to **1 July 2017**).

blocks.title: The scheme at a glance
rows: A quick and inexpensive forum where bank customers can get complaints about certain bank services resolved.
Introduced by the RBI under **Section 35A** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**.
Version in operation (as per the source)
Banking Ombudsman Scheme **2006**, as amended up to 1 July 2017.
The **RBI** (not the Government of India, not any bank).
At the time of writing, **20** Banking Ombudsmen had been appointed, with offices mostly in state capitals.

blocks.title: Banks covered by the 2006 scheme
items: All **Scheduled Commercial Banks**
**Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**
**Scheduled Primary Co-operative Banks**

blocks.title: Scheme years in order
blocks.phrase: 95 begins, 06 rules, 17 amends, 18 adds NBFCs, 21 unites all.
letters: First Banking Ombudsman Scheme (Section 35A, BR Act 1949)
The scheme that stayed in operation for years; Clause 8 lists the grounds
Last amendment of the 2006 scheme (1 July 2017)
Separate Ombudsman Scheme for NBFCs (23 February 2018)
Integrated Ombudsman Scheme joins the separate schemes together

blocks.title: Must-know
blocks.text: The Ombudsman is appointed by the **RBI**. The scheme rests on **Section 35A** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, began in **1995**, and the 2006 version was the one in force (amended up to 2017) before the 2021 integration.

sections.title: Grounds of complaint to the Banking Ombudsman

blocks.text: The grounds fall in two groups: service deficiencies **other than loans and advances**, and deficiencies connected with **loans and advances**. The Ombudsman may also take up any other matter that the RBI specifies from time to time.

blocks.title: Deposits, accounts, charges and facilities
items: Failure or delay in issuing **drafts, pay orders or bankers’ cheques**
Not following the **prescribed working hours**
Refusing to **open a deposit account** without a valid reason
**Levying charges** without adequate prior notice to the customer
Failure or delay in providing a banking facility (other than loans and advances)
**Refusal to close**, or delay in closing, an account
Not following the **fair practices code** adopted by the bank
**Forced closure** of deposit accounts without due notice or sufficient reason
Not following RBI guidelines on the use of **recovery agents** by banks

blocks.title: NRIs, cards, digital banking, pension, taxes and other products
items: Complaints from **NRIs** with accounts in India about remittances from abroad, deposits and other bank matters
Not following RBI instructions on **ATM / debit card and prepaid card** operations
Not following RBI instructions on **credit card** operations (by the bank or its subsidiaries)
Not following RBI instructions on **mobile banking / electronic banking** services
**Non-disbursement or delay** in disbursing **pension**
Refusing or delaying to accept **payment towards taxes**
Not following RBI guidelines on selling **insurance, mutual fund or other third-party** investment products
Any other violation of RBI directives on banking or other services

blocks.title: Grounds related to loans and advances
items: Not following RBI directives on **interest rates**
**Delay** in sanction or disbursement, or ignoring the prescribed time schedule for disposing of loan applications
**Refusing a loan application** without giving valid reasons to the applicant
Not following the **fair practices code for lenders** (or the code of the bank’s commitment to customers)
Not following any other RBI direction or instruction specified for this purpose

blocks.title: Do not confuse
blocks.text: Complaints against a customer’s behaviour, or decisions on CRR, SLR or MSF, are **not** the Ombudsman’s work. The Ombudsman handles **customers’ complaints about deficiency in bank services**, not monetary policy and not bank-versus-customer disputes.

sections.title: How a complaint reaches the Ombudsman

blocks.title: Steps for the customer
items: First complain to the **bank concerned** and keep a record of it.
Wait for the bank’s reply for **one month** from the date the bank receives the complaint.
Approach the Banking Ombudsman if the bank sends **no reply within one month**, or **rejects** the complaint, or the customer is **not satisfied** with the reply.
The Ombudsman examines the matter and the customer gets the outcome.

blocks.title: Journey of a bank complaint
items: Complaint to the bank
Always the first step
Wait one month
Bank must reply within this time
No reply / rejection
Or customer is unhappy with the reply
Banking Ombudsman
Appointed by the RBI

blocks.title: Exam angle
blocks.text: The key period is **one month** of waiting. The customer cannot skip the bank: the Ombudsman is the **next step**, not the first.

Besides the Banking Ombudsman, the RBI introduced an **Ombudsman Scheme for Non-Banking Financial Companies, 2018**. It is a free, quick **apex-level mechanism** for settling complaints of NBFC customers about certain services. The **NBFC Ombudsman** is a senior official appointed by the RBI, and complaints are tested against **Clause 8** of the scheme.

blocks.title: Key facts
rows: **Section 45L** of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

NBFCs (as defined in Section 45-I(f) and registered under Section 45-IA of the RBI Act) that either accept deposits, or have a customer interface with assets of **₹100 crore (one billion rupees)** or more as per the last audited balance sheet, or any size the RBI prescribes.
NBFCs **authorised to accept deposits**; the scheme was to be extended gradually to other identified NBFCs.

blocks.title: Offices of the NBFC Ombudsman
items: Chennai
Kolkata
New Delhi
Mumbai

blocks.title: Banking Ombudsman versus NBFC Ombudsman
rows: Scheduled commercial banks, RRBs, scheduled primary co-operative banks
NBFCs accepting deposits, or with customer interface and assets of ₹100 crore or more
Four: Chennai, Kolkata, New Delhi, Mumbai
One month for the bank’s reply
One month for the NBFC’s reply

blocks.title: Which section for which scheme?
blocks.phrase: Banks live at 35A in the BR Act; NBFCs live at 45L in the RBI Act.
letters: Banking Ombudsman: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
NBFC Ombudsman: Section 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
blocks.note: Both numbers go up (35 to 45) because the NBFC scheme is the newer one, and the act with the older year (1934) holds the number 45.

blocks.title: NBFC Ombudsman offices: CKDM
blocks.phrase: The four metros: Chennai, Kolkata, Delhi, Mumbai.
blocks.note: Think CKDM = the four metro cities. Banking Ombudsman offices are many (state capitals); the NBFC ones are only these four.

blocks.title: Grounds of complaint (Clause 8 of the NBFC scheme)
items: **Non-payment or inordinate delay** in paying interest on deposits
Not following RBI directives on the **rate of interest on deposits**
**Non-repayment or delay** in repaying deposits
**Non-presentation or delay** in presenting **post-dated cheques** given by the customer
Failure to tell the borrower **in writing** the loan amount, terms, annualised interest rate and how it is applied
Failure to give the sanction letter and terms in a **vernacular language** the borrower understands
Failure to give adequate notice of **changes** in sanctioned terms, in a language the borrower understands
Failure or delay in **releasing securities or documents** after all dues are repaid
**Levying charges** without adequate prior notice
Failure to include a legally enforceable **repossession clause** in the loan agreement

Lack of transparency in the agreement on **notice before taking possession**, when notice can be waived, the possession procedure, a **final chance** before sale or auction, how possession is returned, and the sale or auction procedure
Not following **RBI directions** to NBFCs
Not following other provisions of the RBI **Fair Practices Code for NBFCs**

blocks.title: Compensation limits (NBFC scheme)
rows: Limited to the amount arising **directly** from the NBFC’s act or omission, or **₹10 lakh (one million)**, whichever is **lower**.

blocks.title: Procedure
items: The complainant must **first approach the NBFC**.
If the NBFC does **not reply within one month**, **rejects** the complaint, or the complainant is **not satisfied**, the complaint can go to the Ombudsman.
File it with the NBFC Ombudsman in whose **jurisdiction** the NBFC’s **branch or registered office** falls.

blocks.title: Compensation: 10 for the loss, 1 for the pain
blocks.phrase: Ten lakh for the pocket, one lakh for the pain.
letters: = 1 million: cap on compensation for loss (or the direct loss, if lower)
= 0.1 million: extra cap for mental agony and harassment
blocks.note: Conversion help: 1 million = 10 lakh, so 0.1 million = 1 lakh.

blocks.title: Words to watch
blocks.text: The loss cap is the amount arising directly from the NBFC’s act **or** ₹10 lakh, **whichever is lower**. Do not read it as a flat ₹10 lakh payout.

sections.title: Appellate Authority under the NBFC scheme

blocks.text: A complainant who is unhappy with the **award** of the NBFC Ombudsman, or with the **rejection** of the complaint, can go to the **Appellate Authority**. The time limit is **30 days** from receiving the communication of the award or rejection.

blocks.title: What the Appellate Authority can do
items: **Dismiss** the appeal
**Allow** the appeal and **set aside** the award
**Send the matter back** to the NBFC Ombudsman for fresh disposal, following the directions it considers necessary
**Modify** the award and give directions to put the modified award into effect
Pass **any other order** it thinks fit

blocks.text: If the applicant shows sufficient cause for missing the 30-day limit, the Appellate Authority may allow **a further period not exceeding 30 days**.

blocks.title: The 1-30-30 clock
blocks.phrase: One month to reply, thirty days to appeal, thirty more if you have a reason.
letters: Time the NBFC (or bank) gets to reply before you go to the Ombudsman
Time to appeal against the award or rejection
Maximum extra time for appeal if sufficient cause is shown

sections.title: NBFCs: what they are and what they cannot do

blocks.text: A **Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC)** is a company registered under the **Companies Act, 1956** that works in loans and advances, and in acquiring shares, stock, bonds, debentures and other marketable securities (including those issued by the government or a local authority). It may also do **leasing, hire-purchase, insurance business or chit business**.

blocks.title: NBFC versus bank
headers: What it means for an NBFC
rows: No. It finances but does not function as a bank.
May take deposits in forms like fixed deposits; **cannot** accept demand deposits such as savings accounts.
Not allowed to open savings bank accounts.
Not a member of the clearing houses.
Can acquire securities issued by the government or local authorities (it is part of the business).

blocks.title: IFC-NBFC rule
blocks.text: An **Infrastructure Finance Company (IFC) NBFC** must deploy at least **75%** of its total assets in **infrastructure loans**.

blocks.title: Scale-based layers of NBFCs (top to bottom)
items: Top layer
Kept empty unless RBI sees extreme risk
Upper layer (NBFC-UL)
Largest NBFCs and others the RBI identifies
Middle layer (NBFC-ML)
Deposit-takers and those with larger assets
Base layer (NBFC-BL)
Smaller and specialised NBFCs

blocks.text: At the time of the 2022 exam, the RBI’s Upper Layer list had **16** NBFCs, including names such as Bajaj Finance, LIC Housing Finance, Tata Sons, L&T Finance, Muthoot Finance, Shriram Transport, Cholamandalam Investment and Aditya Birla Finance. The list is revised periodically, so treat the count as dated.

From **12 November 2021** the RBI brought in the **Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS)**, following a **One Nation, One Ombudsman** approach. It replaced the earlier separate schemes so that a customer need not figure out which ombudsman to approach.

blocks.title: Schemes merged into the integrated scheme
items: Banking Ombudsman Scheme, **2006**
Ombudsman Scheme for NBFCs, **2018**
Ombudsman Scheme for Digital Transactions, **2019**

blocks.title: Main features (as per the 2021 scheme)
rows: **Deficiency in service** in general, instead of a fixed list of grounds.
Complaints can be filed online, by email or in writing, and are handled through the **Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC)** at **Chandigarh**.
The regulated entity (bank, NBFC or payment participant) has **30 days** to reply before the customer can escalate.
Up to **₹20 lakh** for direct loss, plus up to **₹1 lakh** for loss of time, expenses, harassment and mental agony.
Against the Ombudsman’s decision, to the Appellate Authority within **30 days**.

blocks.title: Keep the timeline straight
blocks.text: The older scheme details above (1995, 2006, 2018) are still asked in exams, but the **integrated scheme of 2021** now covers banks, NBFCs and payment system participants together. Check the latest RBI circulars for any changes after 2021.

revision: Banking Ombudsman is appointed by the **RBI** to settle complaints about deficiency in certain banking services.
Banking Ombudsman Scheme: **Section 35A**, Banking Regulation Act **1949**; started **1995**; 2006 version amended up to **1 July 2017**.
The 2006 scheme covers scheduled commercial banks, RRBs and scheduled primary co-operative banks.
At the time of writing, **20** Banking Ombudsmen with offices mostly in state capitals.
Customer must first complain to the bank, and may approach the Ombudsman after **one month** without a reply, or on rejection or dissatisfaction.
NBFC Ombudsman Scheme: **Section 45L**, RBI Act 1934; in force from **23 February 2018**.
NBFC scheme covers deposit-taking NBFCs, and those with customer interface and assets of **₹100 crore** or more.
NBFC Ombudsman offices: **Chennai, Kolkata, New Delhi, Mumbai**.
NBFC compensation: direct loss or **₹10 lakh**, whichever is lower; up to **₹1 lakh** for mental agony.
Appeal against NBFC Ombudsman award: within **30 days**, extendable by up to **30 days**.
NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits, open savings accounts or join clearing houses.
An **IFC-NBFC** must keep at least **75%** of assets in infrastructure loans.
**Integrated Ombudsman Scheme** of **12 November 2021** merged the Banking (2006), NBFC (2018) and Digital Transactions (2019) schemes.
Under the 2021 scheme: ground is deficiency in service; compensation up to **₹20 lakh** plus **₹1 lakh**; CRPC at **Chandigarh**.
